notes: Upstream-clone debugging task on matplotlib/matplotlib at parent commit 7722dead68f8de43480f1f58386d03396bd5d58e (real upstream issue #28386, fixed upstream by commit e90952ffac668bd5115c4009bf20dd6e595c3cd5). AxLine.get_transform decides whether an axline is horizontal with `np.isclose(slope, 0)`, whose default atol of 1e-8 snaps every slope with |slope| <= 1e-8 to a perfectly horizontal line, so axline((0,0), slope=1e-14) renders with zero tilt (measured dy == 0.0 at the parent). The upstream fix compares `slope == 0` exactly: only a true zero slope is horizontal, tiny slopes keep their tilt (measured dy = 3.69e-12 for slope 1e-14). Shape per the raised-difficulty directive: the image ships the PRISTINE parent tree with NO reproduction, so the agent must author its own failing reproduction (/app/repro.sh, driving the project's own `python3 -m pytest` runner with a scenario test it writes and then removes) as a deliverable before fixing; the verifier runs that repro against the pre-fix tree (must FAIL and print a failing pytest run) and against the repaired tree (must PASS), then the upstream golden regression test test_axline_small_slope (extracted at build time from the fix commit into /opt/golden via a throwaway clone that is rm -rf'd; the fix object is unreachable from the clone: git init + single `git fetch --depth 1 origin <parent-sha>`, rev-list --all --count == 1), a subset of the project's own existing suite nodes that exercise the same file and the axline API (test_axes.py::test_axline_args; test_lines.py::test_axline_setters, test_segment_hits, test_invalid_line_data, test_linestyle_variants), and five authored hidden cases on inputs the upstream test never uses: slope -1e-14 (negative tilt; dy must be negative), slope 5e-9 with a proportionality assertion (dy(5e-9)/dy(1e-14) in (1e3, 1e8), so a fix that clamps every snapped slope to one magnitude is caught — ratio 1 fails; measured ratio ~5e5 on the fixed tree), slope 1e-14 anchored at (1,2) (same magnitude, different anchor), slope 1e-13 (an order of magnitude above the upstream input, upper bound scaled so the case pins magnitude), and a slope-0 constraint case (exactly-zero slope must STILL be horizontal, so a 'remove the zero handling' cheat fix is caught). The hidden cases run both against the repaired tree (all five must pass) and against the pre-fix tree (the four small-slope ones must fail; the slope-0 constraint passes on both). Author-side attack runs confirmed each tightening bites: atol=5e-14 partial snap -> 0 (golden+repro+hidden), magnitude clamp -> 0 (semantic gate + ratio case), tampered /opt/golden -> 0 (sha gate), deleted project test files + pytest.ini -> 0 (provenance byte/untracked gates), untouched container (nop) -> 0; a semantically-equivalent atol=0 formulation correctly scores 1. Semantic provenance gate: HEAD stays the pinned parent, the fix commit is absent from the clone, only lib/matplotlib/lines.py may differ from the parent blobs (byte-level check of every other tracked file, no untracked non-ignored files other than the meson subprojects/.wraplock), and the buggy `np.isclose(slope` pattern must be gone from lines.py. Dependency pins identical to sibling matplotlib tasks (chainplate-anchorage, ballast-longshore): meson-python 0.16.0, pybind11 3.1.0, setuptools-scm 10.2.3, ninja 1.13.2, meson 1.12.0, setuptools 84.0.0, numpy 2.5.3, contourpy 1.3.3, cycler 0.12.1, kiwisolver 1.5.1, fonttools 4.65.0, packaging 26.3, certifi 2026.7.22, pillow 12.3.0, pyparsing 3.1.4 (must stay <3.2.0: matplotlib's pytest config turns warnings into errors and pyparsing 3.2.0's resetCache deprecation otherwise aborts collection), python-dateutil 2.9.0.post0, pytest 8.4.2. Editable meson-python install (freetype/harfbuzz/qhull vendored as meson subprojects, compiled at image build time; gcc-14 from Debian trixie build-essential); at trial time the agent edits .py files only and every pytest run triggers the fast incremental meson editable loader. Build-time fail-closed check asserts the parent-direction symptom (dy == 0.0) inside the image; the fix direction is re-confirmed inside the final task image by the oracle run and by the author's both-directions container run before registration. The pure-Python one-line fix means no rebuild between tree states, so every verifier phase runs in seconds at 1 CPU. Honest difficulty: the raised shape (no reproduction given, agent authors /app/repro.sh, localises the slope branch inside a large real tree, subtle floating-point snapping semantics) lands the rubric at 12 (medium); the fix itself is a single line.
